args.key_findings: (1) landing_bonus is completely dead: 0.0% activation rate, mean=0.0 in eval episodes — v4's threshold relaxation (sigma 0.3→1.0, cutoffs 0.3→0.5, w_land 80→20) had zero effect. (2) proximity_delta dominates at 83.8% signed share / 86.7% magnitude share, driving generated_reward to +0.59 while original_env_reward is −1.50 and eval score is −111.88. Agent learns to approach origin but crashes, terminating early (~68 steps, 20/20 early terminal).
args.component_anomalies: landing_bonus: 0% active, mean 0.0 — the component never fires because contact (left_contact/right_contact) never occurs. The agent terminates before reaching the pad. The relaxation addressed thresholds on velocity/angle/distance AFTER contact, but contact itself is the bottleneck — no contact means the bonus is structurally unreachable.
args.mechanism_hypothesis: The agent exploits proximity_delta by diving toward the origin, accumulating +56 episode-sum from proximity_delta. This crash-diving yields early termination (~68 steps) and very negative eval scores (−111.88). No intermediate shaping reward exists to encourage controlled approach, so the only positive signal (proximity_delta) is perversely maximized by crashing fast. The landing_bonus cannot counterbalance because contact is never reached.
args.decision_implication: Redesign landing_bonus: replace contact-gated bonus with a proximity-gated approach-quality reward that activates BEFORE contact (e.g., reward low velocity + low angle when dist < 0.5, scaled by dist). The contact-gated bonus can remain as a completion bonus but is insufficient alone. Proximity_delta may also need a velocity-cap to penalize fast approaches.
